title: HTTP
hook: Once the connection is open, your request needs a shared language — that language is HTTP.

steps.caption: Your browser sends a structured request: a method, a path, and headers.

nodeCaptions.client: GET means "just give me this" — one of a handful of HTTP methods.

steps.caption: The server replies with a status code and, usually, the content you asked for.

nodeCaptions.server: 200 means success. A different number — like 404 — tells you something else happened.

takeaways: HTTP is the format both sides agree to use: a method and path going one way, a status code and content coming back.
The status code tells you what happened before you even look at the content — 200 is success, 404 is "not found."
HTTP rides on top of the TCP connection — the handshake opens the pipe, HTTP is what flows through it.

quiz.question: What does an HTTP status code like 200 or 404 tell you?
choices: The outcome of the request — success, not found, error, and so on
quiz.explanation: Status codes are a compact way for the server to say what happened, independent of whatever content came back with it.
